newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Surge in British summer tourists seen in Algarve.
newsitem.headline: Surge in British summer tourists seen in Algarve.

text.p: The Algarve sun-and-sand region of southern Portugal is expecting a surge in visitors from Britain this summer after a dismal 1996, a senior tourism official said on Wednesday.

"Bookings by British tourists are much better than last year because of the stronger U.K. economy and the recent increase in the pound against the escudo," said Eliderico Viegas, head of the Association of Hotels and Tourism Businesses of the Algarve.
He told Reuters an earlier than usual launch of promotional campaigns by tour operators had also pushed up demand.

Bookings of 1997 summer package holidays in the Algarve by the British, the main source of visitors, were up by 30 percent compared to last year, official figures showed. Bookings by Germans, the second source of revenue, were stagnant.

Last year the Algarve suffered a sharp drop in British visitors, who account for almost a third of all tourists to the region, as many were deterred by a stronger escudo and uncertainties about job security at home.
Tourism in the Algarve brings in a total of some eight million visitors and generates 600 billion escudos ($3.7 billion) in revenue a year, about 60 percent of Portugal's total tourism receipts.
The region has long stretches of sandy beach, many golf courses, marinas and a well-developed tourist infrastructure ranging from five-star hotels to basic self-catering apartments.
